Prestige gear · rethink · 21 Sep 2026
What's wrong with prestige gear today 1. Five kinds of gift (clock · ring · wearable · Barn gift · keepsake) in four homes; no surface says ‘a Wallow gives you this’. The rank sheet, the only one that knows the rank, shows none of it. 2. ‘Prestige gear’ names one of the five — the wearables — counted on a Me row and filtered inside the Shop tab. Earned status lives in the shop. 3. Three hats in six ranks: a W6 pig wears four of six; the set never reads as a set. 4. The Barn gift is also for sale (50–175 snouts) — a coupon, not a mark. 5. Keepsakes are the real inscribed marks, and they skip W2 · W4 · W5. Rings stop at 5; W6 repeats W5. 6. The ring is the only public mark and never touches the living pig.

The Barn owns prestige. A Wallow shelf shows keepsake · wearable · gift per rank; visitors see it. The rank sheet's rungs open the shelf; the Closet filter and Me row are cut. Costs a tap to wear anything, and asks the Barn — a Connect surface — to be a trophy case too.

Recommendation: D — regalia, one home Keep the six finished wearables, make them one outfit, and let the rank sheet be the only place prestige is explained: ring · regalia piece · keepsake per rung, ‘wear it’ on earned rungs. Cut the Closet prestige filter and the Me ‘Prestige gear’ row (the Wallow row says ‘W2 · 2 of 6 regalia’). Barn decor gifts drop off the ladder and are simply sold; keepsakes fill W2 · W4 · W5 (three new frames). Serves Collect (a set that completes on the pig) and craft (one home, doors elsewhere). Data: re-slot two catalog rows and add three keepsake rows; Barn gifts untouched.
